patterns: APPSC asks cause-effect one-liners: wind deflection to the right in NH = rotation; variation in day length = inclined axis.
Coriolis statement sets (apparent force, right in NH, large-scale weather) are the most frequent multi-statement item.
Tide timing arithmetic (next high tide ~52 minutes later) appears in APPSC Group-1.
Common trap: day and night attributed to revolution, or seasons to rotation; key is rotation vs revolution + tilt.
App uses many long statement and 'how many' sets; PYQs are shorter, mostly 2-3 statements or direct cause questions.
